blogs.title: When Sepsis Isn't Just Sepsis: Unmasking Thrombotic Microangiography After Stabilization
blogs.description: Explore the dangerous diagnostic trap where evolving Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS) mimics resolving Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC). We analyze why a clinician might miss the transition from sepsis-driven organ failure to complement-mediated TMA once coagulation parameters normalize, emphasizing the specific red flags (persistent thrombocytopenia + rising hemolysis indices) that demand immediate re-evaluation.

blogs.title: Beyond TTP and Stool Toxins: Navigating the Diagnostic Labyrinth of Adult Acute Kidney Injury
blogs.description: Break down the stepwise algorithm for distinguishing between Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP), STEC-HUS, and Complement-Mediated HUS (CM-HUS). Using this case, we examine why a normal ADAMTS13 (>10%) does not guarantee 'safe' status, how to interpret borderline values, and why a negative Shiga toxin PCR isn't enough to stop looking for mechanical causes of hemolysis when renal failure dominates.

blogs.title: The Dog Bite Paradox: Canimals, Capsules, and Complement Dysregulation
blogs.description: Delve into the pathophysiological link between *Capnocytophaga canimorsus* bacteremia and catastrophic complement activation. Discuss the clinical paradox where complement is needed to clear this encapsulated organism but becomes the weapon causing endothelial destruction in susceptible hosts, and review why *C. canimorsus* is emerging as a distinct infectious trigger for atypical HUS independent of known genetic mutations.

blogs.title: Eclipsing the Infection Risk: Timing Eculizumab Therapy in Active Gram-Negative Septicaemia
blogs.description: Address one of medicine's toughest dilemmas: administering life-saving complement inhibition (eculizumab) during an active or recently cleared bacterial infection. We evaluate the timing strategies employed here—from holding therapy until sterility versus early empiric dosing—and outline strict protocols for meningococcal/capsule coverage and vaccine timing when treating CM-HUS triggered by organisms like *Capnocytophaga*.

blogs.title: Normal C3/C4 Levels Don't Rule It Out: Interpreting Lab Traps in Complement-Mediated Disease
blogs.description: Challenge the common misconception that low classic/complement levels are required for diagnosing atypical HUS. Explain why C3 and C4 consumption patterns vary widely in acquired vs. genetic forms and how functional assays (AH50) or dynamic response to therapy often carry more weight than static serum complements when confirming a diagnosis of exclusion.
